description: Comprehensive question bank derived from General Science and Technology study material for FDA & SDA competitive examination preparation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the universe?

options.A: The totality of space, time, matter and energy, including all galaxies, stars, planets and radiation
options.B: Only the Milky Way galaxy and its stars
options.C: The Solar System and its planets

questions.explanation: The universe is the totality of space, time, matter and energy, including all galaxies, stars, planets, radiation and other physical contents.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a galaxy?

options.A: A vast gravitationally bound system of stars, stellar remnants, gas, dust and dark matter
options.B: A single star with orbiting planets
options.C: A cloud of gas in the atmosphere
options.D: A group of asteroids between Mars and Jupiter

questions.explanation: A galaxy is a vast gravitationally bound system of stars, stellar remnants, gas, dust and dark matter.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Where is the Solar System located within the Milky Way?

options.A: In the Orion Spur, between major spiral arms
options.B: At the exact centre of the galaxy
options.C: In the galactic halo

questions.explanation: The Solar System lies in the Orion Spur, between major spiral arms of the Milky Way.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a star?

options.A: A massive, luminous sphere of hot plasma that produces energy mainly through nuclear fusion in its core
options.B: A rocky body orbiting the Sun
options.C: A frozen body with a tail
options.D: A natural satellite of a planet

questions.explanation: A star is a massive, luminous sphere of hot plasma that produces energy mainly through nuclear fusion in its core.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: According to the International Astronomical Union (IAU), what defines a planet?

options.A: A body that orbits the Sun, is nearly round due to its gravity, and has cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit
options.B: Any body that orbits a star and has moons
options.C: A body that orbits the Sun and has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood

questions.explanation: Under the IAU definition, a planet orbits the Sun, is nearly round due to gravity, and has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun.

options.A: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
options.B: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus
options.C: Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
options.D: Mercury, Earth, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus

questions.explanation: The eight planets in order from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a dwarf planet?

options.A: A body that orbits the Sun, is nearly round, has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood and is not a satellite
options.B: A small planet with no moons
options.C: A planet that orbits another planet
options.D: A moon of a larger planet

questions.explanation: A dwarf planet orbits the Sun, is nearly round, has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood and is not a satellite.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following are the five officially recognised dwarf planets by the IAU?

options.A: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake
options.B: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Titan and Makemake
options.C: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Ganymede
options.D: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Triton

questions.explanation: The five officially recognised dwarf planets by the IAU are Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a natural satellite?

options.A: A naturally occurring body that orbits a planet or dwarf planet
options.B: A human-made object placed in orbit
options.C: A small planet orbiting the Sun

questions.explanation: A natural satellite is a naturally occurring body that orbits a planet or dwarf planet; Earth's Moon is an example.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Solar System?

options.A: The Sun and all objects gravitationally bound to it, including planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets, meteoroids and dust
options.B: Only the Sun and the eight planets
options.C: The Milky Way galaxy

questions.explanation: The Solar System includes the Sun and all objects gravitationally bound to it, including planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets, meteoroids and dust.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Sun?

options.A: The star at the centre of the Solar System; its gravity governs planetary orbits and its radiation is the principal energy source for Earth's climate and life
options.B: A planet that emits light
options.C: A moon of Earth
options.D: A comet at the centre of the Solar System

questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the centre of the Solar System; its gravity governs planetary orbits and its radiation is the principal energy source for Earth's climate and life.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the approximate age of the Sun?

options.A: About 4.6 billion years
options.B: About 1 million years
options.C: About 13.8 billion years

questions.explanation: The Sun is approximately 4.6 billion years old.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Moon?

options.A: Earth's only permanent natural satellite; it reflects sunlight and strongly influences ocean tides
options.B: A planet that orbits Earth
options.C: A star that orbits Earth

questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's only permanent natural satellite; it reflects sunlight and strongly influences ocean tides.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are asteroids?

options.A: Small rocky or metallic bodies orbiting the Sun, most of which are found in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter
options.B: Icy bodies that develop tails near the Sun
options.C: Natural satellites of planets
options.D: Fragments of meteoroids that reach the ground

questions.explanation: Asteroids are small rocky or metallic bodies orbiting the Sun, most of which are found in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a comet?

options.A: An icy small Solar System body that can develop a glowing coma and tails when solar heating releases gas and dust near the Sun
options.B: A rocky body in the asteroid belt
options.C: A natural satellite of a planet
options.D: A star that moves across the sky

questions.explanation: A comet is an icy small Solar System body that can develop a glowing coma and tails when solar heating releases gas and dust near the Sun.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a meteoroid?

options.A: A small natural solid object in space, smaller than an asteroid by common usage
options.B: The streak of light produced when an object enters the atmosphere
options.C: A fragment that reaches the ground

questions.explanation: A meteoroid is a small natural solid object in space, smaller than an asteroid by common usage.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a meteor?

options.A: The streak of light produced when a meteoroid enters an atmosphere and heats the surrounding gas; commonly called a shooting star
options.B: A solid object in space
options.C: A fragment that reaches the ground

questions.explanation: A meteor is the streak of light produced when a meteoroid enters an atmosphere and heats the surrounding gas; commonly called a shooting star.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a meteorite?

options.A: A fragment of a meteoroid or asteroid that survives passage through the atmosphere and reaches the ground
options.B: The streak of light in the sky
options.C: A small object in space

questions.explanation: A meteorite is a fragment of a meteoroid or asteroid that survives passage through the atmosphere and reaches the ground.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a constellation?

options.A: A formally defined region of the sky; familiar star patterns such as Orion are commonly used as visual groupings
options.B: A group of planets orbiting a star
options.C: A cluster of galaxies

questions.explanation: A constellation is a formally defined region of the sky; familiar star patterns such as Orion are commonly used as visual groupings.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What causes a solar eclipse?

options.A: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks all or part of the Sun as seen from some locations on Earth
options.B: Earth passes between the Sun and Moon
options.C: The Sun passes between Earth and Moon
options.D: The Moon passes through Earth's shadow

questions.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks all or part of the Sun as seen from some locations on Earth.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main types of solar eclipse?

options.A: Total, partial, annular and hybrid
options.B: Total, partial and penumbral
options.C: Total, annular and penumbral

questions.explanation: The main types of solar eclipse are total, partial, annular and hybrid solar eclipses.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What causes a lunar eclipse?

options.A: Earth passes between the Sun and Moon, and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon when the three bodies are aligned near a lunar node
options.B: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth
options.C: The Sun passes between Earth and Moon
options.D: The Moon passes in front of a planet

questions.explanation: A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth passes between the Sun and Moon, and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon when the three bodies are aligned near a lunar node.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main types of lunar eclipse?

options.A: Total, partial and penumbral
options.B: Total, partial, annular and hybrid
options.C: Total, annular and hybrid

questions.explanation: The main types of lunar eclipse are total, partial and penumbral lunar eclipses.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why does a solar eclipse not occur every new moon?

options.A: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees to Earth's orbital plane, so the Sun, Moon and Earth usually do not align precisely
options.B: The Moon is too far from Earth
options.C: The Sun moves too fast

questions.explanation: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees to Earth's orbital plane, so the Sun, Moon and Earth usually do not align precisely.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What causes the phases of the Moon?

options.A: The changing fraction of the Moon's sunlit hemisphere visible from Earth as the Moon orbits Earth
options.B: Earth's shadow falling on the Moon
options.C: The Moon's changing distance from Earth

questions.explanation: The phases of the Moon are caused by the changing fraction of the Moon's sunlit hemisphere visible from Earth as the Moon orbits Earth.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the approximate period of the Moon's phases from one new moon to the next?

options.A: About 29.5 days, called the synodic month
options.B: About 27.3 days, called the sidereal month
options.C: About 24 hours

questions.explanation: The period from one new moon to the next is about 29.5 days, called the synodic month.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Earth's rotation?

options.A: The spinning of Earth on its axis, taking about 24 hours relative to the Sun and producing the daily cycle of day and night
options.B: Earth's orbital motion around the Sun
options.C: The movement of Earth's tectonic plates

questions.explanation: Earth's rotation is the spinning of Earth on its axis, taking about 24 hours relative to the Sun and producing the daily cycle of day and night.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Earth's revolution?

options.A: Earth's orbital motion around the Sun, taking about 365.24 days and defining the length of a year
options.B: The spinning of Earth on its axis
options.C: The movement of the Moon around Earth
options.D: The movement of the Solar System around the galaxy

questions.explanation: Earth's revolution is its orbital motion around the Sun, taking about 365.24 days and defining the length of a year.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What causes seasons on Earth?

options.A: Earth's axial tilt of about 23.5 degrees combined with its revolution around the Sun, changing solar angle and day length in each hemisphere
options.B: Earth's changing distance from the Sun
options.C: The Moon's gravitational pull
options.D: Variations in the Sun's energy output

questions.explanation: Seasons are caused by Earth's axial tilt of about 23.5 degrees combined with its revolution around the Sun, changing solar angle and day length in each hemisphere.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Are seasons mainly caused by Earth's changing distance from the Sun?

options.A: No. Axial tilt is the main cause; Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January
options.B: Yes, distance is the primary cause
options.C: Yes, but only in the Southern Hemisphere
options.D: No, seasons are caused by the Moon's orbit

questions.explanation: Seasons are not mainly caused by Earth's changing distance from the Sun. Axial tilt is the main cause; Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an artificial satellite?

options.A: A human-made object deliberately placed in orbit around Earth or another celestial body
options.B: A natural body orbiting a planet
options.C: A small planet orbiting the Sun

questions.explanation: An artificial satellite is a human-made object deliberately placed in orbit around Earth or another celestial body.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main types of artificial satellites by application?

options.A: Communication, meteorological/weather, navigation, Earth-observation/remote-sensing, scientific research, astronomy, and military or surveillance satellites
options.B: Only communication and weather satellites
options.C: Only navigation and military satellites

questions.explanation: The main types of artificial satellites by application include communication, meteorological/weather, navigation, Earth-observation/remote-sensing, scientific research, astronomy, and military or surveillance satellites.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What do communication satellites do?

options.A: Relay television, telephone, internet and data signals over large areas; many operate in geostationary or other specialised orbits
options.B: Observe clouds and storms
options.C: Transmit precise timing and ranging signals for navigation
options.D: Obtain information about Earth's surface without direct contact

questions.explanation: Communication satellites relay television, telephone, internet and data signals over large areas; many operate in geostationary or other specialised orbits.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What do weather satellites do?

options.A: Observe clouds, water vapour, storms, temperature and other atmospheric or oceanic variables to support forecasting and climate monitoring
options.B: Relay television and telephone signals
options.C: Provide positioning and navigation services

questions.explanation: Weather satellites observe clouds, water vapour, storms, temperature and other atmospheric or oceanic variables to support forecasting and climate monitoring.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What do navigation satellites do?

options.A: Transmit precise timing and ranging signals that allow receivers to calculate position, velocity and time; examples include GPS and India's NavIC
options.B: Relay television and internet signals
options.C: Observe weather patterns

questions.explanation: Navigation satellites transmit precise timing and ranging signals that allow receivers to calculate position, velocity and time; examples include GPS and India's NavIC.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is remote sensing?

options.A: Obtaining information about Earth's surface or atmosphere without direct physical contact, using sensors on satellites, aircraft or drones
options.B: Using telescopes to observe distant stars
options.C: Measuring temperature with a thermometer

questions.explanation: Remote sensing is obtaining information about Earth's surface or atmosphere without direct physical contact, using sensors on satellites, aircraft or drones.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are common applications of remote sensing satellites?

options.A: Agriculture, forestry, land-use mapping, water resources, urban planning, disaster management, ocean monitoring, mineral exploration and environmental assessment
options.B: Only weather forecasting
options.C: Only military surveillance

questions.explanation: Common applications of remote sensing satellites include agriculture, forestry, land-use mapping, water resources, urban planning, disaster management, ocean monitoring, mineral exploration and environmental assessment.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is geostationary orbit?

options.A: A circular equatorial orbit with a period equal to Earth's rotation, making a satellite appear fixed above one point on the equator
options.B: An orbit passing near Earth's poles
options.C: An orbit relatively close to Earth

questions.explanation: A geostationary orbit is a circular equatorial orbit with a period equal to Earth's rotation, making a satellite appear fixed above one point on the equator.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a polar orbit?

options.A: An orbit passing near Earth's poles, allowing the satellite to observe different longitudes as Earth rotates beneath it
options.B: An orbit fixed above one point on the equator
options.C: An orbit around the Sun

questions.explanation: A polar orbit passes near Earth's poles, allowing the satellite to observe different longitudes as Earth rotates beneath it.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a low Earth orbit (LEO)?

options.A: An orbit relatively close to Earth, commonly used by Earth-observation satellites, crewed spacecraft and many broadband constellations
options.B: An orbit fixed above one point on the equator
options.C: An orbit passing near Earth's poles

questions.explanation: A low Earth orbit (LEO) is an orbit relatively close to Earth, commonly used by Earth-observation satellites, crewed spacecraft and many broadband constellations.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is space exploration?

options.A: The investigation of outer space using telescopes, robotic spacecraft, landers, rovers, orbiters and human spaceflight
options.B: The study of Earth's atmosphere
options.C: The exploration of the deep ocean

questions.explanation: Space exploration is the investigation of outer space using telescopes, robotic spacecraft, landers, rovers, orbiters and human spaceflight.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is human spaceflight?

options.A: Space missions in which people travel beyond Earth's atmosphere, conduct operations in space and return safely
options.B: Missions using only robotic spacecraft
options.C: The study of stars from Earth

questions.explanation: Human spaceflight refers to space missions in which people travel beyond Earth's atmosphere, conduct operations in space and return safely.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a space station?

options.A: A crewed spacecraft in orbit designed for extended human habitation, scientific research and technology testing
options.B: A launch vehicle used to send satellites to space
options.C: A telescope on Earth used to observe stars
options.D: A satellite used only for communication

questions.explanation: A space station is a crewed spacecraft in orbit designed for extended human habitation, scientific research and technology testing.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a space telescope?

options.A: A telescope operating above Earth's atmosphere to observe electromagnetic radiation without atmospheric distortion or absorption in selected wavelength bands
options.B: A telescope used only to observe the Moon
options.C: A telescope placed on a mountain top
options.D: A device used to launch satellites

questions.explanation: A space telescope operates above Earth's atmosphere to observe electromagnetic radiation without atmospheric distortion or absorption in selected wavelength bands.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is ISRO?

options.A: The Indian Space Research Organisation, India's national space agency, responsible for space research, launch vehicles, satellites and space applications
options.B: The International Space Research Organisation
options.C: The Indian Scientific Rocket Office
options.D: The Institute of Space Research Operations

questions.explanation: ISRO stands for the Indian Space Research Organisation, India's national space agency, responsible for space research, launch vehicles, satellites and space applications.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is NASA?

options.A: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration, the United States government agency for civilian space and aeronautics research
options.B: The National Aerospace and Science Agency
options.C: The North American Space Association
options.D: The National Astronomy and Satellite Agency

questions.explanation: NASA is the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, the United States government agency for civilian space and aeronautics research.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is ESA?

options.A: The European Space Agency, an intergovernmental organisation coordinating the space activities of its member states and partners
options.B: The Earth Science Association
options.C: The European Satellite Agency

questions.explanation: ESA is the European Space Agency, an intergovernmental organisation coordinating the space activities of its member states and partners.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Chandrayaan-1?

options.A: India's first lunar mission, launched in 2008; its instruments provided important evidence for water/hydroxyl molecules on the lunar surface
options.B: India's first Mars mission
options.C: India's first solar mission

questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-1 was India's first lunar mission, launched in 2008; its instruments provided important evidence for water/hydroxyl molecules on the lunar surface.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Chandrayaan-2?

options.A: India's 2019 lunar mission comprising an orbiter, lander and rover; the lander did not achieve a soft landing, while the orbiter continued scientific operations
options.B: India's 2023 lunar mission that achieved a soft landing
options.C: India's first Mars mission

questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-2 was India's 2019 lunar mission comprising an orbiter, lander and rover; the lander did not achieve a soft landing, while the orbiter continued scientific operations.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Chandrayaan-3?

options.A: India's lunar mission that achieved a successful soft landing near the lunar south polar region on 23 August 2023; the lander was named Vikram and the rover Pragyan
options.B: India's first lunar mission launched in 2008
options.C: India's Mars Orbiter Mission

questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 achieved a successful soft landing near the lunar south polar region on 23 August 2023; the lander was named Vikram and the rover Pragyan.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Mangalyaan?

options.A: The Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), India's first interplanetary mission, launched in 2013 and inserted into Mars orbit in 2014
options.B: India's first lunar mission
options.C: India's first solar mission

questions.explanation: Mangalyaan is the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), India's first interplanetary mission, launched in 2013 and inserted into Mars orbit in 2014.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Aditya-L1?

options.A: India's first dedicated solar observatory mission, placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point to study the solar atmosphere, solar wind and space weather
options.B: India's first lunar mission
options.C: India's Mars Orbiter Mission

questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated solar observatory mission, placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point to study the solar atmosphere, solar wind and space weather.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Gaganyaan?

options.A: India's human spaceflight programme intended to demonstrate the capability to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit and return them safely
options.B: India's lunar mission
options.C: India's Mars mission

questions.explanation: Gaganyaan is India's human spaceflight programme intended to demonstrate the capability to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit and return them safely.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Vyommitra?

options.A: A half-humanoid robot developed for the Gaganyaan programme to support uncrewed mission testing and evaluate systems before human spaceflight
options.B: India's first lunar rover
options.C: A satellite used for navigation
options.D: A launch vehicle developed by ISRO

questions.explanation: Vyommitra is a half-humanoid robot developed for the Gaganyaan programme to support uncrewed mission testing and evaluate systems before human spaceflight.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is PSLV?

options.A: Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, ISRO's versatile launch vehicle widely used for Earth-observation, scientific and commercial satellite missions and interplanetary payloads
options.B: Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle
options.C: Launch Vehicle Mark-3

questions.explanation: PSLV stands for Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, ISRO's versatile launch vehicle widely used for Earth-observation, scientific and commercial satellite missions and interplanetary payloads.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is GSLV?

options.A: Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, designed to place heavier payloads into geosynchronous transfer orbit and other required orbits, using an indigenous cryogenic upper stage in later versions
options.B: Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle
options.C: Launch Vehicle Mark-3

questions.explanation: GSLV stands for Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, designed to place heavier payloads into geosynchronous transfer orbit and other required orbits, using an indigenous cryogenic upper stage in later versions.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is LVM3?

options.A: Launch Vehicle Mark-3, ISRO's heavy-lift launch vehicle, formerly called GSLV Mk III; it is intended for heavy satellites and the Gaganyaan human-spaceflight programme
options.B: Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle
options.C: Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle

questions.explanation: LVM3 stands for Launch Vehicle Mark-3, ISRO's heavy-lift launch vehicle, formerly called GSLV Mk III; it is intended for heavy satellites and the Gaganyaan human-spaceflight programme.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between PSLV and LVM3?

options.A: PSLV is a medium-lift vehicle widely used for polar and Sun-synchronous orbits; LVM3 is a heavier launcher with greater payload capacity, including missions to geostationary transfer orbit
options.B: PSLV is heavier than LVM3
options.C: LVM3 is used only for polar orbits
options.D: PSLV is a reusable launch vehicle

questions.explanation: PSLV is a medium-lift vehicle widely used for polar and Sun-synchronous orbits; LVM3 is a heavier launcher with greater payload capacity, including missions to geostationary transfer orbit.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a cryogenic rocket engine?

options.A: An engine that uses propellants stored at extremely low temperatures, typically liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, to produce high-performance thrust
options.B: An engine that uses solid propellants
options.C: An engine that uses room-temperature liquid propellants
options.D: An engine that uses nuclear energy

questions.explanation: A cryogenic rocket engine uses propellants stored at extremely low temperatures, typically liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, to produce high-performance thrust.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is NavIC?

options.A: Navigation with Indian Constellation, India's regional satellite navigation system providing positioning, navigation and timing services over India and a surrounding region
options.B: India's weather satellite system
options.C: India's communication satellite network

questions.explanation: NavIC stands for Navigation with Indian Constellation, India's regional satellite navigation system providing positioning, navigation and timing services over India and a surrounding region.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is SPADEX?

options.A: ISRO's Space Docking Experiment, which demonstrated autonomous rendezvous and docking between two small spacecraft, a key technology for complex future missions
options.B: India's solar observatory mission
options.C: India's Mars Orbiter Mission

questions.explanation: SPADEX is ISRO's Space Docking Experiment, which demonstrated autonomous rendezvous and docking between two small spacecraft, a key technology for complex future missions.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is NISAR?

options.A: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar, a joint Earth-observation mission using L-band and S-band radar to study changes in land, ice and ecosystems
options.B: India's navigation satellite system
options.C: India's solar observatory mission

questions.explanation: NISAR stands for NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar, a joint Earth-observation mission using L-band and S-band radar to study changes in land, ice and ecosystems.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are major applications of space technology in India?

options.A: Communication, television, weather forecasting, navigation, disaster warning, agriculture, fisheries, water management, mapping, telemedicine, education and national security
options.B: Only communication and television
options.C: Only weather forecasting

questions.explanation: Major applications of space technology in India include communication, television, weather forecasting, navigation, disaster warning, agriculture, fisheries, water management, mapping, telemedicine, education and national security.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is atomic energy?

options.A: Energy associated with the structure and interactions of atoms, including electronic and nuclear energy; in power generation, the term often refers to nuclear energy
options.B: Energy stored in chemical bonds
options.C: Energy from the Sun

questions.explanation: Atomic energy is energy associated with the structure and interactions of atoms, including electronic and nuclear energy; in power generation, the term often refers to nuclear energy.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nuclear energy?

options.A: Energy released from changes in atomic nuclei, especially nuclear fission or fusion
options.B: Energy released from chemical reactions
options.C: Energy from the Sun's light

questions.explanation: Nuclear energy is energy released from changes in atomic nuclei, especially nuclear fission or fusion.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nuclear fission?

options.A: The splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus, such as uranium-235, into smaller nuclei, releasing energy and neutrons
options.B: The joining of light atomic nuclei
options.C: The decay of a radioactive nucleus
options.D: The capture of an electron by a nucleus

questions.explanation: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus, such as uranium-235, into smaller nuclei, releasing energy and neutrons.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a nuclear chain reaction?

options.A: A self-sustaining sequence in which neutrons released by one fission event cause further fissions
options.B: A series of fusion reactions in the Sun
options.C: A chemical reaction in a nuclear reactor

questions.explanation: A nuclear chain reaction is a self-sustaining sequence in which neutrons released by one fission event cause further fissions.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nuclear fusion?

options.A: The joining of light atomic nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy when the products have greater binding energy per nucleon; it powers the Sun and stars
options.B: The splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus
options.C: The decay of a radioactive nucleus
options.D: The capture of a neutron by a nucleus

questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion is the joining of light atomic nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy when the products have greater binding energy per nucleon; it powers the Sun and stars.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the main difference between fission and fusion?

options.A: Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion combines light nuclei. Both can release nuclear energy
options.B: Fission combines light nuclei; fusion splits heavy nuclei
options.C: Fission releases energy; fusion does not
options.D: Fusion occurs only in nuclear reactors; fission occurs only in stars

questions.explanation: Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion combines light nuclei. Both can release nuclear energy.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a nuclear reactor?

options.A: A system in which a controlled nuclear fission chain reaction is maintained to produce heat, usually for electricity generation or research
options.B: A device that produces nuclear fusion for power
options.C: A machine that accelerates particles
options.D: A device that stores nuclear waste

questions.explanation: A nuclear reactor is a system in which a controlled nuclear fission chain reaction is maintained to produce heat, usually for electricity generation or research.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main components of a nuclear reactor?

options.A: Fuel, moderator in many reactor designs, control rods, coolant, reactor vessel or core structure, shielding and safety systems
options.B: Fuel, solar panels and batteries
options.C: Fuel, turbine and generator only

questions.explanation: The main components of a nuclear reactor include fuel, moderator in many reactor designs, control rods, coolant, reactor vessel or core structure, shielding and safety systems; exact designs vary.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nuclear fuel?

options.A: Fissile or fertile material used in a reactor, such as uranium-235, plutonium-239 or uranium-233 in suitable fuel cycles
options.B: Coal used in a nuclear reactor
options.C: Heavy water used as fuel

questions.explanation: Nuclear fuel is fissile or fertile material used in a reactor, such as uranium-235, plutonium-239 or uranium-233 in suitable fuel cycles.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is uranium?

options.A: A naturally occurring radioactive heavy metal; uranium-235 is fissile and uranium-238 is fertile and can be converted into plutonium-239 in reactors
options.B: A non-radioactive metal used in reactors
options.C: A gas used as coolant
options.D: A material used for control rods

questions.explanation: Uranium is a naturally occurring radioactive heavy metal; uranium-235 is fissile and uranium-238 is fertile and can be converted into plutonium-239 in reactors.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is thorium?

options.A: A naturally occurring radioactive element; thorium-232 is fertile, not itself fissile with thermal neutrons, and can be converted into fissile uranium-233
options.B: A fissile material used directly in reactors
options.C: A moderator used in reactors

questions.explanation: Thorium is a naturally occurring radioactive element; thorium-232 is fertile, not itself fissile with thermal neutrons, and can be converted into fissile uranium-233.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a moderator in a nuclear reactor?

options.A: A material that slows fast neutrons to thermal energies to improve the likelihood of fission in reactors designed for thermal-neutron operation
options.B: A material that absorbs neutrons to stop the reaction
options.C: A fluid that removes heat from the core
options.D: A material that reflects neutrons back into the core

questions.explanation: A moderator in a nuclear reactor is a material that slows fast neutrons to thermal energies to improve the likelihood of fission in reactors designed for thermal-neutron operation.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are control rods?

options.A: Neutron-absorbing components, often containing boron, cadmium or hafnium, used to regulate or shut down the fission chain reaction
options.B: Rods that slow down neutrons
options.C: Rods that remove heat from the core

questions.explanation: Control rods are neutron-absorbing components, often containing boron, cadmium or hafnium, used to regulate or shut down the fission chain reaction.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a coolant in a nuclear reactor?

options.A: A fluid or other medium that removes heat from the reactor core and transfers it to a steam or power-conversion system
options.B: A material that slows down neutrons
options.C: A material that absorbs neutrons
options.D: A material that contains nuclear fuel

questions.explanation: A coolant in a nuclear reactor is a fluid or other medium that removes heat from the reactor core and transfers it to a steam or power-conversion system.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a nuclear power plant?

options.A: A facility that uses heat from a nuclear reactor to produce steam or another working fluid that drives a turbine-generator to generate electricity
options.B: A facility that uses solar energy to generate electricity
options.C: A facility that uses wind energy to generate electricity
options.D: A facility that stores nuclear waste

questions.explanation: A nuclear power plant is a facility that uses heat from a nuclear reactor to produce steam or another working fluid that drives a turbine-generator to generate electricity.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is radioactivity?

options.A: The spontaneous transformation of unstable atomic nuclei, accompanied by emission of particles or electromagnetic radiation
options.B: The splitting of a heavy nucleus by a neutron
options.C: The joining of light nuclei
options.D: The absorption of light by an atom

questions.explanation: Radioactivity is the spontaneous transformation of unstable atomic nuclei, accompanied by emission of particles or electromagnetic radiation.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are alpha particles?

options.A: Helium nuclei consisting of two protons and two neutrons; they have low penetration but can cause serious harm if radioactive material is inhaled or ingested
options.B: High-speed electrons
options.C: High-energy electromagnetic radiation

questions.explanation: Alpha particles are helium nuclei consisting of two protons and two neutrons; they have low penetration but can cause serious harm if radioactive material is inhaled or ingested.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are beta particles?

options.A: High-speed electrons or positrons emitted in certain nuclear transformations; they have greater penetration than alpha particles but less than gamma rays in general
options.B: Helium nuclei
options.C: High-energy electromagnetic radiation

questions.explanation: Beta particles are high-speed electrons or positrons emitted in certain nuclear transformations; they have greater penetration than alpha particles but less than gamma rays in general.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are gamma rays?

options.A: High-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted by nuclear transitions; they are highly penetrating and require dense shielding
options.B: Helium nuclei
options.C: High-speed electrons

questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted by nuclear transitions; they are highly penetrating and require dense shielding.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is half-life?

options.A: The time required for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay; it is characteristic of a particular radionuclide
options.B: The time required for all radioactive nuclei to decay
options.C: The time required for a nucleus to split
options.D: The time required for a reactor to start up

questions.explanation: Half-life is the time required for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay; it is characteristic of a particular radionuclide.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is ionising radiation?

options.A: Radiation with sufficient energy to remove electrons from atoms or molecules, creating ions; it includes alpha, beta, gamma, X-rays and neutrons
options.B: Radiation that cannot penetrate any material
options.C: Radiation emitted only by the Sun

questions.explanation: Ionising radiation has sufficient energy to remove electrons from atoms or molecules, creating ions; it includes alpha, beta, gamma, X-rays and neutrons.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the main applications of nuclear science in medicine?

options.A: Diagnostic imaging using radioisotopes, cancer radiotherapy, sterilisation of medical equipment and research in nuclear medicine
options.B: Only cancer treatment
options.C: Only sterilisation of equipment

questions.explanation: The main applications of nuclear science in medicine include diagnostic imaging using radioisotopes, cancer radiotherapy, sterilisation of medical equipment and research in nuclear medicine.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nuclear medicine?

options.A: A medical speciality using radioactive tracers for diagnosis and radionuclide therapies for selected diseases
options.B: A branch of medicine that uses only X-rays
options.C: A branch of medicine that uses only ultrasound
options.D: A branch of medicine that uses only surgery

questions.explanation: Nuclear medicine is a medical speciality using radioactive tracers for diagnosis and radionuclide therapies for selected diseases.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How are radioisotopes used in agriculture?

options.A: They support mutation breeding, studies of nutrient and water uptake, pest control through sterile insect techniques, food irradiation and soil research
options.B: They are used only as fertilisers
options.C: They are used only as pesticides
options.D: They are used only for irrigation

questions.explanation: Radioisotopes support mutation breeding, studies of nutrient and water uptake, pest control through sterile insect techniques, food irradiation and soil research.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is food irradiation?

options.A: Controlled exposure of food to ionising radiation to reduce pathogens and pests, delay sprouting or ripening and extend shelf life; it does not make food radioactive
options.B: A process that makes food radioactive
options.C: A process that adds nutrients to food

questions.explanation: Food irradiation is controlled exposure of food to ionising radiation to reduce pathogens and pests, delay sprouting or ripening and extend shelf life; it does not make food radioactive.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nuclear safety?

options.A: The prevention of accidents and limitation of their consequences through sound design, operation, regulation, emergency preparedness and safety culture
options.B: The prevention of nuclear weapons proliferation
options.C: The management of nuclear waste only
options.D: The physical security of nuclear facilities only

questions.explanation: Nuclear safety is the prevention of accidents and limitation of their consequences through sound design, operation, regulation, emergency preparedness and safety culture.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is radiation protection?

options.A: Measures to prevent or reduce unnecessary exposure to ionising radiation, guided by justification, optimisation and dose limitation for regulated exposures
options.B: The design of radiation shields only
options.C: The monitoring of radiation levels only
options.D: The treatment of radiation injuries only

questions.explanation: Radiation protection refers to measures to prevent or reduce unnecessary exposure to ionising radiation, guided by justification, optimisation and dose limitation for regulated exposures.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the three basic principles of radiation protection?

options.A: Justification of practices, optimisation of protection (ALARA) and dose limitation for individuals in regulated exposure situations
options.B: Time, distance and shielding
options.C: Containment, ventilation and filtration

questions.explanation: The three basic principles of radiation protection are justification of practices, optimisation of protection (ALARA: as low as reasonably achievable) and dose limitation for individuals in regulated exposure situations.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is radioactive waste?

options.A: Waste containing radionuclides above regulatory clearance levels, requiring management according to its activity, half-life, heat generation and physical/chemical form
options.B: Any waste produced in a nuclear facility
options.C: Waste from hospitals only

questions.explanation: Radioactive waste is waste containing radionuclides above regulatory clearance levels, requiring management according to its activity, half-life, heat generation and physical/chemical form.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is nuclear waste managed?

options.A: Through characterisation, segregation, treatment, conditioning, secure storage and, where appropriate, disposal in engineered facilities; high-level waste requires long-term isolation
options.B: By dumping it in the ocean
options.C: By burning it in the atmosphere
options.D: By storing it indefinitely without treatment

questions.explanation: Nuclear waste is managed through characterisation, segregation, treatment, conditioning, secure storage and, where appropriate, disposal in engineered facilities; high-level waste requires long-term isolation.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is India's three-stage nuclear power programme?

options.A: A strategy designed to use natural uranium in pressurised heavy-water reactors, develop plutonium-based fast breeder reactors, and ultimately utilise thorium to produce uranium-233
options.B: A programme to build only solar power plants
options.C: A programme to import nuclear reactors from other countries
options.D: A programme to develop nuclear weapons only

questions.explanation: India's three-stage nuclear power programme is a strategy designed to use natural uranium in pressurised heavy-water reactors, develop plutonium-based fast breeder reactors, and ultimately utilise thorium to produce uranium-233.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why is thorium important to India's nuclear programme?

options.A: India has substantial thorium resources, particularly in monazite-bearing coastal sands; the long-term programme seeks to use thorium through a uranium-233 fuel cycle
options.B: Thorium is fissile and can be used directly in reactors
options.C: India imports all its thorium
options.D: Thorium is used only in research reactors

questions.explanation: India has substantial thorium resources, particularly in monazite-bearing coastal sands; the long-term programme seeks to use thorium through a uranium-233 fuel cycle.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)?

options.A: The Government of India's department responsible for developing and applying nuclear energy and related technologies for power, research, medicine, agriculture and industry
options.B: The nuclear safety regulator
options.C: The company that operates nuclear power plants
options.D: A research centre based in Trombay

questions.explanation: The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) is the Government of India's department responsible for developing and applying nuclear energy and related technologies for power, research, medicine, agriculture and industry.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is BARC?

options.A: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, a major DAE research institution based at Trombay, Mumbai, working in nuclear science, reactor technology and related fields
options.B: Bharat Atomic Regulatory Commission
options.C: Bhabha Atomic Reactor Corporation

questions.explanation: BARC stands for Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, a major DAE research institution based at Trombay, Mumbai, working in nuclear science, reactor technology and related fields.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is NPCIL?

options.A: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, a public sector enterprise under DAE responsible for design, construction, commissioning and operation of nuclear power plants in India
options.B: National Power Corporation of India Limited
options.C: Nuclear Plant Construction and Installation Limited
options.D: National Physics and Chemistry Institute Limited

questions.explanation: NPCIL stands for Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, a public sector enterprise under DAE responsible for design, construction, commissioning and operation of nuclear power plants in India.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is AERB?

options.A: Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, India's nuclear and radiation safety regulator, responsible for regulatory oversight of radiation facilities and nuclear installations within its mandate
options.B: Atomic Energy Research Board
options.C: Atomic Energy Reactor Board

questions.explanation: AERB stands for Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, India's nuclear and radiation safety regulator, responsible for regulatory oversight of radiation facilities and nuclear installations within its mandate.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between BARC and NPCIL?

options.A: BARC is primarily a research and development centre; NPCIL is the public sector company responsible for operating and developing nuclear power plants
options.B: BARC operates nuclear power plants; NPCIL conducts research
options.C: Both are regulatory bodies

questions.explanation: BARC is primarily a research and development centre; NPCIL is the public sector company responsible for operating and developing nuclear power plants.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between AERB and DAE?

options.A: DAE is the government department responsible for atomic energy development; AERB performs regulatory safety functions and is institutionally distinct from plant operators
options.B: AERB is the government department; DAE is the regulator
options.C: Both are research institutions

questions.explanation: DAE is the government department responsible for atomic energy development; AERB performs regulatory safety functions and is institutionally distinct from plant operators.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a pressurised heavy-water reactor (PHWR)?

options.A: A reactor design that uses heavy water as moderator and coolant and can use natural uranium fuel in India's established reactor fleet
options.B: A reactor that uses light water as moderator and enriched uranium as fuel
options.C: A reactor that uses graphite as moderator and natural uranium as fuel
options.D: A reactor that uses fast neutrons and no moderator

questions.explanation: A pressurised heavy-water reactor (PHWR) is a reactor design that uses heavy water as moderator and coolant and can use natural uranium fuel in India's established reactor fleet.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a fast breeder reactor?

options.A: A reactor designed to produce more fissile material than it consumes, by converting fertile material into fissile material using fast neutrons
options.B: A reactor that uses slow neutrons to breed fuel
options.C: A reactor that uses heavy water as moderator
options.D: A reactor that produces electricity from fusion

questions.explanation: A fast breeder reactor is a reactor designed to produce more fissile material than it consumes, by converting fertile material into fissile material using fast neutrons.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR)?

options.A: A 500 MWe sodium-cooled fast breeder reactor project at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, developed by BHAVINI as part of India's second-stage nuclear programme
options.B: A 500 MWe pressurised heavy-water reactor at Trombay
options.C: A 500 MWe light-water reactor at Kudankulam
options.D: A 500 MWe thorium reactor at Mumbai

questions.explanation: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) is a 500 MWe sodium-cooled fast breeder reactor project at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, developed by BHAVINI as part of India's second-stage nuclear programme.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is biotechnology?

options.A: The use of living organisms, cells, biological systems or their components to develop products and processes for human use
options.B: The study of rocks and minerals
options.C: The use of computers to analyse data
options.D: The study of stars and planets

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells, biological systems or their components to develop products and processes for human use.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is traditional biotechnology?

options.A: Use of organisms and biological processes in practices such as fermentation, selective breeding, cheese-making, bread-making and composting
options.B: Application of molecular biology and genetic engineering
options.C: Use of computers to analyse biological data

questions.explanation: Traditional biotechnology is the use of organisms and biological processes in practices such as fermentation, selective breeding, cheese-making, bread-making and composting.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is modern biotechnology?

options.A: Application of molecular biology, cell biology, genetic engineering, genomics and related technologies to modify or analyse biological systems
options.B: Use of organisms in fermentation and selective breeding
options.C: Use of computers to store biological data
options.D: Use of microscopes to observe cells

questions.explanation: Modern biotechnology is the application of molecular biology, cell biology, genetic engineering, genomics and related technologies to modify or analyse biological systems.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is genetic engineering?

options.A: Direct modification of an organism's genetic material using biotechnology methods to introduce, remove or alter DNA sequences
options.B: Selective breeding of plants and animals
options.C: Study of the structure of cells
options.D: Use of computers to analyse genomes

questions.explanation: Genetic engineering is the direct modification of an organism's genetic material using biotechnology methods to introduce, remove or alter DNA sequences.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is recombinant DNA technology?

options.A: A method of joining DNA from different sources and introducing the resulting DNA molecule into a host system for replication or expression
options.B: A method of sequencing DNA
options.C: A method of amplifying DNA

questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA technology is a method of joining DNA from different sources and introducing the resulting DNA molecule into a host system for replication or expression.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the basic steps in recombinant DNA technology?

options.A: Identify and isolate a gene, cut or assemble DNA using suitable enzymes or methods, join it to a vector, introduce it into a host, select successful cells and express or analyse the gene
options.B: Only isolate a gene and introduce it into a host
options.C: Only cut DNA with restriction enzymes

questions.explanation: The basic steps in recombinant DNA technology include identifying and isolating a gene, cutting or assembling DNA using suitable enzymes or methods, joining it to a vector, introducing it into a host, selecting successful cells and expressing or analysing the gene.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a plasmid?

options.A: A small, usually circular DNA molecule separate from the bacterial chromosome, often used as a vector in genetic engineering
options.B: A type of virus
options.C: A protein that cuts DNA
options.D: An enzyme that joins DNA fragments

questions.explanation: A plasmid is a small, usually circular DNA molecule separate from the bacterial chromosome, often used as a vector in genetic engineering.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a restriction enzyme?

options.A: An enzyme that recognises specific DNA sequences and cuts DNA at or near those sites
options.B: An enzyme that joins DNA fragments
options.C: An enzyme that amplifies DNA

questions.explanation: A restriction enzyme is an enzyme that recognises specific DNA sequences and cuts DNA at or near those sites.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is DNA ligase?

options.A: An enzyme that joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds in the DNA backbone
options.B: An enzyme that cuts DNA at specific sequences
options.C: An enzyme that amplifies DNA

questions.explanation: DNA ligase is an enzyme that joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds in the DNA backbone.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is gene cloning?

options.A: Production of multiple copies of a specific DNA sequence, commonly by inserting it into a vector and replicating it in host cells or by amplification methods
options.B: Production of a genetically identical organism
options.C: Sequencing of a genome
options.D: Editing of a gene using CRISPR

questions.explanation: Gene cloning is the production of multiple copies of a specific DNA sequence, commonly by inserting it into a vector and replicating it in host cells or by amplification methods.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is DNA fingerprinting?

options.A: Analysis of variable DNA regions to distinguish individuals or establish biological relationships; it is used in forensic science, paternity testing and identification
options.B: A technique to amplify DNA
options.C: A technique to edit genes
options.D: A technique to sequence a genome

questions.explanation: DNA fingerprinting is the analysis of variable DNA regions to distinguish individuals or establish biological relationships; it is used in forensic science, paternity testing and identification.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is PCR?

options.A: Polymerase chain reaction, a laboratory technique that amplifies a selected DNA segment through repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing and extension
options.B: A technique for sequencing DNA
options.C: A technique for editing genes

questions.explanation: PCR stands for polymerase chain reaction, a laboratory technique that amplifies a selected DNA segment through repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing and extension.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Who developed PCR?

options.A: Kary Mullis developed the PCR method in the 1980s; he received the 1993 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the invention
options.B: James Watson
options.C: Francis Crick

questions.explanation: Kary Mullis developed the PCR method in the 1980s; he received the 1993 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the invention.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is genome sequencing?

options.A: Determining the order of nucleotide bases in an organism's DNA or in a selected region of its genome
options.B: Amplifying a DNA segment
options.C: Editing a gene

questions.explanation: Genome sequencing is determining the order of nucleotide bases in an organism's DNA or in a selected region of its genome.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is genomics?

options.A: The study of an organism's entire genome, including its structure, function, variation and interactions
options.B: The study of proteins
options.C: The study of cells

questions.explanation: Genomics is the study of an organism's entire genome, including its structure, function, variation and interactions.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is proteomics?

options.A: The large-scale study of the proteins produced by a cell, tissue or organism, including their abundance, structure and function
options.B: The study of genomes
options.C: The study of genes

questions.explanation: Proteomics is the large-scale study of the proteins produced by a cell, tissue or organism, including their abundance, structure and function.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is genetic modification?

options.A: A deliberate change to an organism's genetic material using breeding or molecular techniques; in common modern usage it often refers to genetic engineering
options.B: A natural mutation in an organism
options.C: A change in an organism's environment
options.D: A change in an organism's behaviour

questions.explanation: Genetic modification is a deliberate change to an organism's genetic material using breeding or molecular techniques; in common modern usage it often refers to genetic engineering.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a genetically modified organism (GMO)?

options.A: An organism whose genetic material has been altered using modern biotechnology in a way that does not occur through conventional mating or natural recombination
options.B: An organism that has naturally mutated
options.C: An organism produced by selective breeding only
options.D: An organism that has been cloned

questions.explanation: A genetically modified organism (GMO) is an organism whose genetic material has been altered using modern biotechnology in a way that does not occur through conventional mating or natural recombination.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a genetically modified crop?

options.A: A crop developed using genetic engineering to introduce a specific trait, such as insect resistance, herbicide tolerance or altered nutritional composition
options.B: A crop developed through conventional breeding only
options.C: A crop grown without pesticides

questions.explanation: A genetically modified crop is a crop developed using genetic engineering to introduce a specific trait, such as insect resistance, herbicide tolerance or altered nutritional composition.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is Bt cotton?

options.A: Cotton genetically engineered to produce insecticidal proteins derived from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, providing protection against certain bollworm pests
options.B: Cotton that is resistant to all pests
options.C: Cotton that is grown without pesticides
options.D: Cotton that is produced by conventional breeding

questions.explanation: Bt cotton is cotton genetically engineered to produce insecticidal proteins derived from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, providing protection against certain bollworm pests.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Does Bt cotton control every cotton pest?

options.A: No. It targets specific susceptible insect pests; sucking pests and other pests may still require integrated pest management
options.B: Yes, it controls all pests
options.C: Yes, it controls sucking pests only

questions.explanation: Bt cotton does not control every cotton pest. It targets specific susceptible insect pests; sucking pests and other pests may still require integrated pest management.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is gene therapy?

options.A: A medical approach that treats or prevents disease by adding, altering or regulating genetic material in a patient's cells
options.B: A technique to edit plant genes
options.C: A technique to amplify DNA
options.D: A technique to sequence a genome

questions.explanation: Gene therapy is a medical approach that treats or prevents disease by adding, altering or regulating genetic material in a patient's cells.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between somatic and germline gene therapy?

options.A: Somatic therapy targets body cells and is not normally inherited by offspring; germline modification affects reproductive cells or embryos and can be inherited
options.B: Somatic therapy affects reproductive cells; germline therapy affects body cells
options.C: Both are inherited by offspring

questions.explanation: Somatic gene therapy targets body cells and is not normally inherited by offspring; germline modification affects reproductive cells or embryos and can be inherited.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are stem cells?

options.A: Undifferentiated or partially differentiated cells capable of self-renewal and of developing into specialised cell types
options.B: Cells that have lost the ability to divide
options.C: Cells that are found only in plants
options.D: Cells that are found only in the brain

questions.explanation: Stem cells are undifferentiated or partially differentiated cells capable of self-renewal and of developing into specialised cell types.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are embryonic stem cells?

options.A: Pluripotent cells derived from the early embryo that can develop into nearly all cell types of the body
options.B: Cells found only in adult bone marrow
options.C: Cells that can only develop into blood cells
options.D: Cells that are found only in plants

questions.explanation: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent cells derived from the early embryo that can develop into nearly all cell types of the body.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are adult stem cells?

options.A: Stem cells found in developed tissues, usually with more limited differentiation potential; examples include haematopoietic stem cells in bone marrow
options.B: Stem cells derived from the early embryo
options.C: Stem cells that can develop into any cell type
options.D: Stem cells found only in plants

questions.explanation: Adult stem cells are stem cells found in developed tissues, usually with more limited differentiation potential; examples include haematopoietic stem cells in bone marrow.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is tissue culture?

options.A: Growth of cells, tissues or organs under controlled, sterile conditions on a suitable nutrient medium
options.B: Growth of whole plants in soil
options.C: Culture of microorganisms in a fermenter only
options.D: Culture of animal cells in a living organism

questions.explanation: Tissue culture is the growth of cells, tissues or organs under controlled, sterile conditions on a suitable nutrient medium.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is plant tissue culture?

options.A: In vitro growth of plant cells, tissues or organs under sterile conditions; it is widely used for rapid multiplication and production of disease-free planting material
options.B: Growth of plants in a greenhouse
options.C: Growth of plants in hydroponics

questions.explanation: Plant tissue culture is the in vitro growth of plant cells, tissues or organs under sterile conditions; it is widely used for rapid multiplication and production of disease-free planting material.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is micropropagation?

options.A: Rapid in vitro multiplication of plants from small explants, often producing many genetically similar plantlets
options.B: Propagation of plants by seeds
options.C: Propagation of plants by cuttings

questions.explanation: Micropropagation is the rapid in vitro multiplication of plants from small explants, often producing many genetically similar plantlets.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is cloning?

options.A: Production of a genetically near-identical copy of a DNA sequence, cell or organism; the exact meaning depends on the biological level
options.B: Production of a genetically unique organism
options.C: Sequencing of a genome
options.D: Editing of a gene using CRISPR

questions.explanation: Cloning is the production of a genetically near-identical copy of a DNA sequence, cell or organism; the exact meaning depends on the biological level.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is reproductive cloning?

options.A: Production of an organism genetically very similar to a donor through techniques such as somatic cell nuclear transfer; Dolly the sheep was a famous example
options.B: Production of multiple copies of a DNA sequence
options.C: Production of a genetically unique organism
options.D: Production of stem cells from an embryo

questions.explanation: Reproductive cloning is the production of an organism genetically very similar to a donor through techniques such as somatic cell nuclear transfer; Dolly the sheep was a famous example.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is CRISPR-Cas9?

options.A: A genome-editing system adapted from a bacterial defence mechanism; guide RNA directs the Cas9 enzyme to a target DNA sequence for cutting and subsequent editing
options.B: A technique to amplify DNA
options.C: A technique to sequence DNA
