questions.explanation: CRISPR-Cas9 is a genome-editing system adapted from a bacterial defence mechanism; guide RNA directs the Cas9 enzyme to a target DNA sequence for cutting and subsequent editing.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are possible applications of CRISPR gene editing?

options.A: Research on gene function, development of disease models, crop improvement and potential treatments for selected genetic disorders; safety and ethical review are essential
options.B: Only crop improvement
options.C: Only treatment of genetic disorders

questions.explanation: Possible applications of CRISPR gene editing include research on gene function, development of disease models, crop improvement and potential treatments for selected genetic disorders; safety and ethical review are essential.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is bioinformatics?

options.A: Use of computing, statistics and information science to store, analyse and interpret biological data such as DNA, RNA and protein sequences
options.B: The study of biological systems without computers
options.C: The study of cells using microscopes
options.D: The study of genes using chemical methods

questions.explanation: Bioinformatics is the use of computing, statistics and information science to store, analyse and interpret biological data such as DNA, RNA and protein sequences.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a biosensor?

options.A: A device that combines a biological recognition element with a transducer to detect a target substance and produce a measurable signal
options.B: A sensor used to measure temperature
options.C: A sensor used to measure pressure
options.D: A sensor used to measure light

questions.explanation: A biosensor is a device that combines a biological recognition element with a transducer to detect a target substance and produce a measurable signal.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a biopharmaceutical?

options.A: A medicinal product produced using biological sources or processes, such as recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, vaccines and some cell or gene therapies
options.B: A medicine made by chemical synthesis only
options.C: A medicine made from minerals
options.D: A medicine made from plants only

questions.explanation: A biopharmaceutical is a medicinal product produced using biological sources or processes, such as recombinant proteins, monoclonal antibodies, vaccines and some cell or gene therapies.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a vaccine?

options.A: A biological preparation that trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen or antigen and develop protective immune responses
options.B: A medicine that kills bacteria directly
options.C: A medicine that kills viruses directly
options.D: A medicine that treats genetic disorders

questions.explanation: A vaccine is a biological preparation that trains the immune system to recognise a pathogen or antigen and develop protective immune responses.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the major types of vaccines?

options.A: Live attenuated, inactivated, subunit/recombinant protein, toxoid, viral-vector, nucleic-acid (mRNA or DNA) and conjugate vaccines
options.B: Only live attenuated and inactivated vaccines
options.C: Only mRNA and DNA vaccines

questions.explanation: The major types of vaccines include live attenuated, inactivated, subunit/recombinant protein, toxoid, viral-vector, nucleic-acid (mRNA or DNA) and conjugate vaccines.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is biotechnology used in medicine?

options.A: In vaccine development, insulin and other recombinant medicines, diagnostics, gene therapy, monoclonal antibodies, personalised medicine and disease research
options.B: Only in vaccine development
options.C: Only in diagnostics

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is used in medicine in vaccine development, insulin and other recombinant medicines, diagnostics, gene therapy, monoclonal antibodies, personalised medicine and disease research.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is biotechnology used in agriculture?

options.A: In crop improvement, tissue culture, marker-assisted breeding, pest and disease resistance, biofertilisers, biopesticides and stress-tolerant varieties
options.B: Only in crop improvement
options.C: Only in pest control

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is used in agriculture in crop improvement, tissue culture, marker-assisted breeding, pest and disease resistance, biofertilisers, biopesticides and stress-tolerant varieties.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is biotechnology used in industry?

options.A: In fermentation, enzyme production, food processing, biofuels, biodegradable materials, pharmaceuticals and industrial biocatalysis
options.B: Only in food processing
options.C: Only in biofuel production

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is used in industry in fermentation, enzyme production, food processing, biofuels, biodegradable materials, pharmaceuticals and industrial biocatalysis.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is biotechnology used in environmental protection?

options.A: In bioremediation, wastewater treatment, biosensors, waste decomposition and development of biological methods to reduce pollution
options.B: Only in wastewater treatment
options.C: Only in bioremediation

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is used in environmental protection in bioremediation, wastewater treatment, biosensors, waste decomposition and development of biological methods to reduce pollution.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is bioremediation?

options.A: Use of microorganisms, plants or biological enzymes to remove, degrade or detoxify environmental contaminants
options.B: Use of chemicals to treat wastewater
options.C: Use of filters to remove pollutants
options.D: Use of incineration to destroy waste

questions.explanation: Bioremediation is the use of microorganisms, plants or biological enzymes to remove, degrade or detoxify environmental contaminants.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are ethical concerns in biotechnology?

options.A: Safety, informed consent, privacy of genetic data, equitable access, ecological effects, animal welfare, patent ownership, germline editing and possible misuse
options.B: Only safety concerns
options.C: Only privacy concerns

questions.explanation: Ethical concerns in biotechnology include safety, informed consent, privacy of genetic data, equitable access, ecological effects, animal welfare, patent ownership, germline editing and possible misuse.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is biosafety?

options.A: Principles, containment practices and regulatory measures designed to prevent unintended exposure to biological agents or their accidental release
options.B: The safety of biological weapons
options.C: The safety of laboratory equipment only
options.D: The safety of patients in hospitals only

questions.explanation: Biosafety refers to principles, containment practices and regulatory measures designed to prevent unintended exposure to biological agents or their accidental release.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Human Genome Project?

options.A: An international research programme that produced a reference sequence and map of the human genome; the original project was declared complete in 2003
options.B: A project to clone human beings
options.C: A project to sequence the genomes of all animals
options.D: A project to develop gene therapy for all diseases

questions.explanation: The Human Genome Project is an international research programme that produced a reference sequence and map of the human genome; the original project was declared complete in 2003.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between gene and genome?

options.A: A gene is a functional DNA sequence; a genome is the complete genetic material of an organism or cell
options.B: A gene is the complete genetic material; a genome is a functional DNA sequence
options.C: A gene is found only in animals; a genome is found only in plants
options.D: Both refer to the same thing

questions.explanation: A gene is a functional DNA sequence; a genome is the complete genetic material of an organism or cell.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nanotechnology?

options.A: The science and engineering of materials and devices at the nanoscale, commonly involving structures with dimensions of roughly 1-100 nanometers
options.B: The study of large-scale machines
options.C: The study of stars and planets

questions.explanation: Nanotechnology is the science and engineering of materials and devices at the nanoscale, commonly involving structures with dimensions of roughly 1-100 nanometers.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a nanometre?

options.A: One billionth of a metre, or 10^-9 metre
options.B: One millionth of a metre
options.C: One thousandth of a metre

questions.explanation: A nanometre is one billionth of a metre, or 10^-9 metre.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why can nanomaterials behave differently from bulk materials?

options.A: They have a high surface-area-to-volume ratio and may exhibit size-dependent optical, electrical, magnetic, chemical and mechanical properties
options.B: They are always chemically inert
options.C: They have a low surface-area-to-volume ratio
options.D: They are always denser than bulk materials

questions.explanation: Nanomaterials can behave differently from bulk materials because they have a high surface-area-to-volume ratio and may exhibit size-dependent optical, electrical, magnetic, chemical and mechanical properties.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are nanomaterials?

options.A: Materials with at least one external dimension or internal structure in the nanoscale range, often producing distinctive properties
options.B: Materials with dimensions greater than 1 micrometre
options.C: Materials that are always toxic

questions.explanation: Nanomaterials are materials with at least one external dimension or internal structure in the nanoscale range, often producing distinctive properties.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are nanoparticles?

options.A: Particles with nanoscale dimensions, commonly 1-100 nm in at least one dimension under widely used definitions
options.B: Particles with dimensions greater than 1 micrometre
options.C: Particles that are always toxic

questions.explanation: Nanoparticles are particles with nanoscale dimensions, commonly 1-100 nm in at least one dimension under widely used definitions.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are carbon nanotubes?

options.A: Cylindrical nanostructures formed from rolled graphene sheets, known for high tensile strength and distinctive electrical and thermal properties
options.B: Tubes made of carbon with micrometre-scale diameters
options.C: Tubes made of silicon

questions.explanation: Carbon nanotubes are cylindrical nanostructures formed from rolled graphene sheets, known for high tensile strength and distinctive electrical and thermal properties.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is graphene?

options.A: A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional hexagonal lattice, with high electrical conductivity, strength and flexibility
options.B: A three-dimensional form of carbon
options.C: A compound of carbon and silicon

questions.explanation: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional hexagonal lattice, with high electrical conductivity, strength and flexibility.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is nanomedicine?

options.A: Application of nanoscale materials and devices in diagnosis, drug delivery, imaging, monitoring and treatment
options.B: Application of nanotechnology in agriculture
options.C: Application of nanotechnology in electronics

questions.explanation: Nanomedicine is the application of nanoscale materials and devices in diagnosis, drug delivery, imaging, monitoring and treatment.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is nanotechnology used in medicine?

options.A: In targeted drug delivery, diagnostic imaging, biosensors, antimicrobial coatings, wound dressings and selected cancer-treatment approaches
options.B: Only in drug delivery
options.C: Only in imaging

questions.explanation: Nanotechnology is used in medicine in targeted drug delivery, diagnostic imaging, biosensors, antimicrobial coatings, wound dressings and selected cancer-treatment approaches.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How can nanotechnology be used in agriculture?

options.A: For controlled delivery of fertilisers and pesticides, nanosensors for soil and crop monitoring, seed treatment and improved water-use efficiency; environmental safety must be assessed
options.B: Only for fertiliser delivery
options.C: Only for pesticide delivery

questions.explanation: Nanotechnology can be used in agriculture for controlled delivery of fertilisers and pesticides, nanosensors for soil and crop monitoring, seed treatment and improved water-use efficiency; environmental safety must be assessed.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is nanotechnology used in electronics?

options.A: In miniaturised transistors, memory devices, displays, sensors, conductive materials and high-performance components
options.B: Only in transistors
options.C: Only in memory devices

questions.explanation: Nanotechnology is used in electronics in miniaturised transistors, memory devices, displays, sensors, conductive materials and high-performance components.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How is nanotechnology used in energy?

options.A: In improved battery electrodes, solar cells, fuel-cell catalysts, supercapacitors, hydrogen storage research and energy-efficient coatings
options.B: Only in batteries
options.C: Only in solar cells

questions.explanation: Nanotechnology is used in energy in improved battery electrodes, solar cells, fuel-cell catalysts, supercapacitors, hydrogen storage research and energy-efficient coatings.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How can nanotechnology help water purification?

options.A: Nanomaterials can support filtration, adsorption, photocatalysis, disinfection and contaminant detection; performance and safe disposal must be evaluated
options.B: Only through filtration
options.C: Only through adsorption

questions.explanation: Nanotechnology can help water purification as nanomaterials can support filtration, adsorption, photocatalysis, disinfection and contaminant detection; performance and safe disposal must be evaluated.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are quantum dots?

options.A: Semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical properties depend on their size; they are used in displays, imaging and research
options.B: Tiny particles of metal
options.C: Carbon nanotubes

questions.explanation: Quantum dots are semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical properties depend on their size; they are used in displays, imaging and research.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the risks of nanomaterials?

options.A: Some may enter the body through inhalation, ingestion or skin contact, interact with cells, persist in ecosystems or behave differently from larger forms of the same material
options.B: They are always safe
options.C: They are always dangerous

questions.explanation: Risks of nanomaterials include that some may enter the body through inhalation, ingestion or skin contact, interact with cells, persist in ecosystems or behave differently from larger forms of the same material.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Why is nanomaterial risk assessment difficult?

options.A: Toxicity can depend on size, shape, surface coating, charge, solubility, dose, exposure route and environmental transformation
options.B: Nanomaterials are always toxic
options.C: Nanomaterials are always safe

questions.explanation: Nanomaterial risk assessment is difficult because toxicity can depend on size, shape, surface coating, charge, solubility, dose, exposure route and environmental transformation.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What precautions are used in nanomaterial safety?

options.A: Characterise materials, assess exposure and toxicity, use appropriate containment and protective equipment, label and store materials correctly, and manage waste safely
options.B: Only use protective equipment
options.C: Only label and store materials correctly

questions.explanation: Precautions used in nanomaterial safety include characterising materials, assessing exposure and toxicity, using appropriate containment and protective equipment, labelling and storing materials correctly, and managing waste safely.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is artificial intelligence (AI)?

options.A: The field of developing computer systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence, such as perception, language, reasoning, prediction and decision support
options.B: The field of building physical robots only
options.C: The field of storing data in computers
options.D: The field of connecting computers to the internet

questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the field of developing computer systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence, such as perception, language, reasoning, prediction and decision support.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is machine learning?

options.A: A branch of AI in which systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed with every rule
options.B: A branch of AI that uses rule-based expert systems only
options.C: A branch of AI that focuses on robotics only
options.D: A branch of AI that focuses on natural language only

questions.explanation: Machine learning is a branch of AI in which systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions without being explicitly programmed with every rule.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is deep learning?

options.A: A subset of machine learning that uses multi-layer artificial neural networks to learn complex representations from data
options.B: A subset of AI that uses rule-based systems
options.C: A subset of robotics that uses sensors
options.D: A subset of NLP that uses grammar rules

questions.explanation: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses multi-layer artificial neural networks to learn complex representations from data.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an artificial neural network?

options.A: A computational model made of interconnected processing units, loosely inspired by biological neurons, that learns patterns by adjusting connection weights
options.B: A network of computers connected by cables
options.C: A network of biological neurons in the brain
options.D: A network of sensors in a robot

questions.explanation: An artificial neural network is a computational model made of interconnected processing units, loosely inspired by biological neurons, that learns patterns by adjusting connection weights.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is natural language processing (NLP)?

options.A: AI methods that enable computers to process, analyse, generate and interact using human language
options.B: AI methods that enable computers to recognise images
options.C: AI methods that enable robots to move
options.D: AI methods that enable computers to store data

questions.explanation: Natural language processing (NLP) refers to AI methods that enable computers to process, analyse, generate and interact using human language.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is computer vision?

options.A: AI methods that interpret information from images and videos, such as detecting objects, recognising patterns and analysing scenes
options.B: AI methods that interpret human language
options.C: AI methods that control robot movement

questions.explanation: Computer vision refers to AI methods that interpret information from images and videos, such as detecting objects, recognising patterns and analysing scenes.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is generative AI?

options.A: AI that creates new content—such as text, images, audio, video or code—based on patterns learned from training data and user prompts
options.B: AI that only classifies data
options.C: AI that only predicts numerical values

questions.explanation: Generative AI is AI that creates new content—such as text, images, audio, video or code—based on patterns learned from training data and user prompts.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a large language model (LLM)?

options.A: A neural network trained on large text datasets to process and generate language; many modern LLMs use transformer architectures
options.B: A model that can only translate languages
options.C: A model that can only answer questions
options.D: A model that can only generate images

questions.explanation: A large language model (LLM) is a neural network trained on large text datasets to process and generate language; many modern LLMs use transformer architectures.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a transformer in AI?

options.A: A neural network architecture that uses attention mechanisms to model relationships among elements in sequences and is widely used in language and multimodal models
options.B: A device that changes electrical voltage
options.C: A type of robot

questions.explanation: A transformer in AI is a neural network architecture that uses attention mechanisms to model relationships among elements in sequences and is widely used in language and multimodal models.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a hallucination in generative AI?

options.A: A confident-sounding output that is false, unsupported or fabricated; users should verify important claims against reliable sources
options.B: A visual output generated by AI
options.C: A type of neural network

questions.explanation: A hallucination in generative AI is a confident-sounding output that is false, unsupported or fabricated; users should verify important claims against reliable sources.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an expert system?

options.A: An AI system that uses a knowledge base and inference rules to provide advice or decisions in a specialised domain
options.B: A system that uses neural networks only
options.C: A system that controls robots

questions.explanation: An expert system is an AI system that uses a knowledge base and inference rules to provide advice or decisions in a specialised domain.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is robotics?

options.A: The interdisciplinary field involving the design, construction, programming and operation of robots
options.B: The field of developing computer software
options.C: The field of studying human intelligence
options.D: The field of designing computer networks

questions.explanation: Robotics is the interdisciplinary field involving the design, construction, programming and operation of robots.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an industrial robot?

options.A: A programmable automated machine used in manufacturing tasks such as welding, painting, assembly, packaging and material handling
options.B: A robot that performs household chores
options.C: A robot that explores space

questions.explanation: An industrial robot is a programmable automated machine used in manufacturing tasks such as welding, painting, assembly, packaging and material handling.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a service robot?

options.A: A robot that performs useful tasks for people or equipment outside traditional industrial automation, such as cleaning, delivery or assistance
options.B: A robot used in manufacturing
options.C: A robot used in space exploration
options.D: A robot used in military combat

questions.explanation: A service robot is a robot that performs useful tasks for people or equipment outside traditional industrial automation, such as cleaning, delivery or assistance.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is an autonomous robot?

options.A: A robot that senses its environment and performs tasks with limited direct human control, using onboard computation and control systems
options.B: A robot that is controlled entirely by a human operator
options.C: A robot that is used only in manufacturing
options.D: A robot that is used only in space

questions.explanation: An autonomous robot is a robot that senses its environment and performs tasks with limited direct human control, using onboard computation and control systems.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a humanoid robot?

options.A: A robot designed with a human-like body structure or appearance, often with a head, torso, arms and legs
options.B: A robot designed to look like an animal
options.C: A robot designed for industrial welding
options.D: A robot designed for space exploration

questions.explanation: A humanoid robot is a robot designed with a human-like body structure or appearance, often with a head, torso, arms and legs.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a drone?

options.A: An unmanned aircraft or aerial vehicle operated remotely or autonomously; many use cameras, navigation sensors and onboard computers
options.B: A type of industrial robot
options.C: A type of humanoid robot
options.D: A type of service robot used indoors

questions.explanation: A drone is an unmanned aircraft or aerial vehicle operated remotely or autonomously; many use cameras, navigation sensors and onboard computers.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the Internet of Things (IoT)?

options.A: A network of physical devices embedded with sensors, software and connectivity that collect and exchange data
options.B: A network of computers connected by cables
options.C: A network of social media platforms

questions.explanation: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical devices embedded with sensors, software and connectivity that collect and exchange data.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is a smart device?

options.A: An electronic device with computing and connectivity features that can sense, process data, communicate or respond automatically
options.B: A device that is only manually operated
options.C: A device that has no connectivity
options.D: A device that cannot process data

questions.explanation: A smart device is an electronic device with computing and connectivity features that can sense, process data, communicate or respond automatically.
questions.source: General Science and Technology Study Guide

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is automation?

options.A: Use of technology to perform tasks or processes with reduced human intervention
options.B: Use of technology to increase human intervention
options.C: Use of technology to replace all human workers
options.D: Use of technology to store data only
